newsitem.title: UK: Rank expects improved second half trading.
newsitem.headline: Rank expects improved second half trading.

text.p: British leisure company Rank Plc will increase its share buy-back programme, said chief executive Andrew Teare on Thursday in a statement attached to the group's half year results.

Chairman Sir Denys Henderson said Rank expects an improvement in its performance in the second half of the year after reporting a 12 million pound ($19.2 million) drop to 87 million in profits before tax and exceptionals in the first half.
There is already evidence of a return to a strong video release pattern while a record number of new leisure retailing venues will open in the second half, said Henderson.
One of the main causes of concern in financial circles has been the recent decline in profit from Rank's video duplication business as a result of lower video sales in the United States.
Rank said it plans to open six Hard Rock cafes in the second half, five Odeon multiplex cinemas, four Mecca bingo clubs, 16 Tom Cobleigh pub restaurants and a Warner hotel.

Teare, who joined Rank in April 1996, has raised 1.3 billion pounds ($2.1 billion) from disposals, including the sale of the company's remaining 20 percent stake in the Rank Xerox office equipment venture to Xerox Corporation XRN.N in a deal worth up to 1.0 billion pounds.

Rank said in June it planned to use some of the proceeds to buy back up to 250 million pounds of its own shares. Although the group said it would increase the size of its buy-back in its half year statement, it gave no further details.
Group turnover from continuing operations rose four percent to 853 million in the six months ended June 30, 1997 but operating profit fell two percent to 90 million.
Rank shares closed at 370-1/2 pence on Wednesday. Analysts had forecast pre-tax profits of between 90 and 98 million pounds. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
